title: Stochastic routing latency trace notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick field notes from stochastic (probabilistic) routing experiments—looking at tail latency behavior, burst recovery, and KV-window interactions on long-context requests for Llama/Mistral/Qwen mixed workloads with MoE layers. Goal: capture traces, short hypotheses, and actionable next steps for SRE + runtime team.

Background / motivation:
- We observe occasional 99.9th percentile spikes when MoE routing probability is > 0.6 for certain prompt families (long-context summarization).
- These spikes correlate with: (a) high expert-switch churn, (b) KV cache misses when prefetch window is narrow, (c) CPU-side scheduling delays during route assignment.
- Previous notes focused on deterministic gating; this doc explores stochastic gating (top-k / softmax sampling) used for experimental ensemble diversity and its perf impact.

Environment / baseline:
- HW: p4d.24xlarge equivalent nodes (NVIDIA A100), 8 GPUs per host.
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.12.3 (kernel selector v0.9b), CUDA 11.8.
- Models tested: llama-2-13b-chat, mistral-7b-instruct, qwen-14b-instruct (quantized paths enabled for Qwen).
- MoE config: 64 experts per layer, top-2 routing with stochastic multiplier (p_sample = 0.2, 0.5, 0.8).
- Typical request: 8–12k tokens context + generation 512 tokens.

Observed traces (representative):
- Trace A (p_sample=0.2): 95th=180ms, 99th=320ms, 99.9th=620ms. Spikes correspond to a ~40ms expert load-balancer reassign step (CPU).
- Trace B (p_sample=0.8): 95th=240ms, 99th=560ms, 99.9th=1.4s. Large increase in tail; disk/serialization not implicated.
- Trace C (p_sample=0.5, KV-prefetch-window=16 tokens): 95th=200ms, 99th=380ms, 99.9th=780ms. Observed repeated KV miss sequences overlapping with routing churn.

Trace excerpt (sanitized):
- t0: request received -> tokenization (6ms)
- t1: route sample (top-2 + stochastic) -> dispatch decision (12–18ms median, up to 60ms on spike)
- t2: GPU enqueue & KV prefetch kick-off (2–4ms)
- t3: expert compute start (30–120ms depending on expert size & batching)
- t4: gather/merge & KV writeback (10–50ms)
- tail: CPU routing cleanup & cache evict lock (10–700ms variable, dominant on 99.9th)

Hypotheses and notes:
1) Stochastic sampling increases routing variance, causing more frequent moves of token affinity across experts; this increases cold-start-like behavior for expert-local caches and bursts KV misses.
2) When samples cause many microshifts within a single request (per-token sampling), the runtime's routing assignment path can execute extra synchronization barriers (we saw lock contention on route-table updates).
3) KV-prefetch window interacts non-linearly: smaller windows reduce wasted prefetch but increase misses for churn-heavy sequences; larger windows reduce misses but increase memory pressure and eviction frequency.
4) CPU scheduling: route decision CPU path is sensitive to cooperative scheduling. Under high concurrency, route assignment stalls ~10–80ms.
5) Quantized models (Qwen path) show higher compute variance per expert because of fallback dequantization overhead during kernel selection.

Quick experiments run (commands and notes):
- toggled p_sample across {0.0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.8} with 1000 synthetic long-context requests (same prompt family); collected p50/p95/p99/p999 and per-stage timings.
- ran kernel tracing (TRACY style) with route decision sampling annotated (see linked PR for trace sourcemap).
- increased KV-prefetch-window from 8 -> 32 tokens for p_sample=0.5 and saw 99.9th drop ~25% for llama-2 but memory resident pages + eviction callbacks rose.

Data summary (aggregated):
- p_sample=0.0 (deterministic): 99.9th ~420ms, KV-miss rate baseline 1.8%
- p_sample=0.2: 99.9th ~600ms, KV-miss rate 3.1%
- p_sample=0.5: 99.9th ~780ms, KV-miss rate 5.6%
- p_sample=0.8: 99.9th ~1400ms, KV-miss rate 11.2%
(note: numbers averaged across model family; Qwen skewed higher)

Immediate workarounds to try (low friction):
- Route decision batching: coalesce routing CPU tasks for requests that arrive within 1–2ms windows to amortize routing overhead. Experiment flag: ROUTE_BATCH_MS=2.
- Prefetch window adaptive heuristic: increase prefetch window if route instability metric > threshold. Heuristic: window = min(32, base + floor(instability_score/10)).
- Per-expert warmup cache hold: hold recently used expert activations for short TTL (50–200ms) to absorb micro-churn. Tradeoff: memory.
- Limit per-token sampling frequency: sample per chunk of tokens (e.g., every 8 tokens) rather than every token. Adds determinism.

Longer-term mitigations / infra ideas:
- Move routing decision to asynchronous GPU-side sampler (experimental): reduces CPU gate but requires GPU kernel to expose scatter/gather cheaply.
- Lock-free route table updates using per-CPU local queues + reconciler thread to reduce critical sections.
- Hybrid deterministic-stochastic routing: deterministic assignment for hot tokens identified by a short LRU history, stochastic sampling for cold tokens.
- Improve kernel-selection for quantized Qwen to minimize dequantize overhead on expert entry.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is KV-prefetch window hitting underlying OS page faults during high churn? We saw elevated major fault counters but need perf counters per-host to confirm.
- Does inter-GPU PCIe bandwidth become a factor when many experts cross-device after stochastic sampling? Early traces show small spikes but need targeted microbench.
- How does routing variance impact cached attention key/value layout (tiling)? Might require per-model tiling heuristics.

Action items / next steps:
- (Samira) add microbenchmark that simulates per-token stochastic sampling on a single host and records OS major/minor faults (due 2024-11-09).
- (Diego) prototype ROUTE_BATCH_MS=2 experiment across a 4-host cluster and collect p999 (due 2024-11-06).
- (Priya) run PCIe/host-to-host memory bandwidth microbench for the Qwen routing path (due 2024-11-12).
- (Avery) open follow-up issue to evaluate GPU-side sampler feasibility and prototype scheduling model (JIRA:SR-742).

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- Could we maintain a tiny probabilistic histogram per token-id (rolling 128 tokens) to decide deterministic vs stochastic path? Low memory per token but might reduce churn.
- Consider a short-lived per-request routing buffer that materializes expert assignment then replays it for the next N tokens to reduce per-token decisions.

Appendix: quick profiler snippets (simplified)
- top stall callers (sampled): route_assign_cpu (42%), expert_dispatch_serializer (18%), kv_prefetch_dispatch (15%), kernel_selection (10%), others (15%).

- Example log line (sanitized):
  [2024-10-29T14:23:12.881Z] req=0x7fae4c route_sample p=0.5 chosen=[E12,E3] cpu_ms=58 gpu_enqueue_ms=3 expert_exec_ms=94 kv_miss_seq=2 tail_cleanup_ms=412

References / related docs:
- see PR 1428 for trace collector enhancements (link above)
- related: moe-prefetch-expert-switching-notes.json (older notes; different focus)

Ending thought: stochastic routing gives diversity/quality benefits but introduces a second-order performance problem (tail amplification via cache churn + CPU synchronization). We should prioritize low-friction mitigations (route batching + adaptive prefetch) and run controlled A/Bs with quality metrics to ensure minimal quality loss.
